name: Undo the Last Commit
problem: You accidentally committed files too early, included the wrong files, or made a typo in the commit message. You haven't pushed to the remote repository yet.

steps.title: Move HEAD backward while keeping changes
steps.description: If you haven't pushed yet, you can smoothly undo the commit while keeping your work intact. The `--soft` flag moves the history pointer back by one (`HEAD~1`), but leaves your changes precisely where they were in the staging area.

steps.title: Make your adjustments
steps.description: Now you can add forgotten files, unstage files you didn't mean to include, or fix typos in your code.
steps.code:
git add forgotten-file.js
git reset HEAD accidental-file.css

steps.title: Commit again
steps.description: Create a new commit with the proper files and a correct message.

alternatives.title: Quick message fix (The amend shortcut)
alternatives.description: If you just want to fix the message or add a single file without resetting entirely, use --amend.
alternatives.code:
git add forgotten-file.js
git commit --amend -m "Fixed message and added missing file"
